jack_carter.title: Jack Carter’s golfing life
jack_carter.author: Jack Carter
jack_carter.date_note: Undated personal account supplied 10 November 2026. The reference to 46 years reflects the time of writing.
paragraphs: My first experience with golf was working for Jim Paterson, he was the professional at the time at Tauranga Golf Club. It was 1957 and I was 12 years old. My job was cleaning and buffing the members clubs after each round and storing them away in the sheds. My spare time was spent chipping and putting, while waiting for the members to finish their rounds.

In 1968 my wife Judy and I headed to Canada, and my job allowed me to play golf most days, joining a municipal golf club with two courses, where I received my first handicap of 12. We returned to New Zealand four years later. As Tauranga Golf Club had a closed membership, for the next 3 years I played my golf at Mount Maunganui Golf Club.
New Zealand Golf had a national handicap of 4, which allowed you to join any club in New Zealand.
Playing off a 5 handicap at Mount Maunganui, I worked diligently to obtain the handicap which allowed me to join the Tauranga Golf Club.

After a few years at Tauranga, I joined the committee under the guidance of Maurice Coad, Maurice White, Noel Copestake and Dan Dougherty. This Committee covered all aspects of the club; financials, course development, member groups (male and female), Juniors and Vets. Maurice Coad thought I'd be a good junior convener and asked if I would run the juniors on Sundays, and with New Zealand winning the Eisenhower Golf Trophy in Canada in 1992, junior golf had exploded in NZ, so I said yes.

In the mid 90's after the end of the Spalding Professional Golf Tournament I acquired the Spalding Cup and promoted the Spalding Masters Junior Under 19 mixed golf tournament - 72 holes played over 3 days. Some of the notable people in the fields included the likes of Lydia Ko, Ryan Fox, Josh Geary, Danny Lee, and my son, Jay Carter, who represented NZ at the Junior World Championships in Japan.

My personal achievements at the Tauranga Golf Club were winning the Senior Men's Championship Plate, the Men's Intermediate and Junior Championships and the other memorable feat was shooting a score of 64 off an 8 handicap in a Saturday competition.

Continuing on, I was involved with the BOP Golf alongside Chris McApline as CEO. I managed the Senior Men's Team which saw us travelling from Whangarei to Invercargill and winning three NZ Interprovincial Titles. I then went from Manager to Selector, a position I held for 3 years. Then, with the purchase of a Motorhome, I decided to slow down a bit and enjoy touring New Zealand.
My last committee involvement was three years on the Senior Men's (Vets) Committee.
In 2019 | was made a life member of the Tauranga Golf Club.
I have thoroughly enjoyed my 46 years involvement with the Tauranga Golf Club and all its wonderful members.
jack_carter.intro: From cleaning members’ clubs as a twelve-year-old in 1957 to junior golf, provincial teams and life membership in 2019: Jack Carter tells his own story.
jack_carter.editorial_note: Two occurrences of Maurice Code have been corrected to Maurice Coad on 10 November 2026. Other wording is retained as supplied.

life_member_profiles.name: Elsie Hanna
paragraphs: Elsie arrived in Tauranga in 1922, won the senior championship in 1924 and 1926, and served on the women’s committee from 1926 to 1939. She became the club’s first woman Life Member before 1948.

The supplied profile recalls the practical work behind interclub hospitality: heating water outdoors and preparing refreshments with limited facilities. Its accompanying trophy sheet dates her presentation of the Elsie Hanna Cup to 1948.

life_member_profiles.name: Noel Copestake
paragraphs: Noel joined in 1960 and served as captain, president and a member of the inaugural Board. Elected a Life Member in 1997, he contributed to twilight golf, pennant teams and the volunteers known as the Wednesday Firewood Gang.
The supplied club announcement of 12 April 2016 records his death that morning and remembers his long commitment to practical work around the course.

life_member_profiles.name: Bernie Child
paragraphs: Bernie brought the skills of a machinery contractor to the club’s many volunteer projects. He organised work for the veterans, served as their president in 1995 and built the drinking fountain behind the first tee. His service was recognised with Life Membership in 1997.
life_member_profiles.note: The supplied page is identified as a reproduction from Mowat’s book; this profile provides a route into that existing history rather than a new appointment.

life_member_profiles.name: Hazel Casey
paragraphs: Hazel helped beginners, schoolchildren and women new to golf. The supplied feature remembers a Saturday group known as Hazel’s Girls and her support for the introduction of nine-hole golf.

Mowat records her arrival at Tauranga Golf Club in 1970 and her earlier start on a small farm course near Ōpōtiki. Her childhood teacher was an earlier Jack Carter, the great-grandfather of professional Jay Carter; he should not be confused with Jay’s father, whose personal account is now in this collection.

life_member_profiles.name: Ernie Craig
paragraphs: Ernie’s long service helped secure the administration and development of the Racecourse Reserve. Mowat describes his work on the reserve’s management arrangements and his Life Membership of both the golf and racing clubs.

The supplied newspaper obituary extract adds context about his business and community service, including his work in accountancy and regional organisations. Only the golf and reserve connection is summarised here; the compilation contains page 2 of the original three-page article.

life_member_profiles.name: Peg Copestake
paragraphs: The supplied achievement summary brings together Peg’s playing record, rules knowledge and volunteer service. It records her joining in 1961, her albatross at the sixth hole in 1966, and her work with juniors and new members.

It also records her election as club president in 2001–02, Life Membership in 2005, and a round of 72 on 23 February 2005 when she played to her age. The summary credits Mowat, Bay of Plenty golf and club records, family memorabilia and the Life Membership application compiled by Wendy Hanna.
A separate clipping remembers her achievements in several other sports before and alongside golf.
life_member_profiles.note: The supplied summary’s championship years of 1974, 1979 and 1984 agree with the book’s honour roll on pp. 291–292. The two wins mentioned in the narrative on p. 96 concern interruptions to Una Wickham’s winning sequence before her final championship in 1980.

life_member_profiles.name: H B Lusk
paragraphs: Mowat credits H B Lusk with helping design the course when the club moved to the Racecourse Reserve and records Life Membership in 1948–49.

The supplied compilation includes a biographical clipping headed Harold Lusk, covering his wider career in teaching, cricket and golf. The club history remains the reference for the course-design and Life Membership details.

life_member_profiles.name: A J Mirrielees
paragraphs: Mowat describes A J Mirrielees’s work on the extensive planting programme that helped shape the course. He was among the club’s Life Members honoured before 1948.

The compilation adds an extract from Debbie McCauley’s biography of Alexander James, or Alick, Mirrielees. It places his golfing contribution within a wider life as a pharmacist, photographer and participant in Tauranga’s civic organisations. His photographic work also connects with the early images preserved in this collection.
life_member_profiles.note: The compilation contains an extract from the biography, not the complete ten-page original.

life_member_profiles.name: Phyll Sandlant
paragraphs: Phyll led the local promotion of women’s nine-hole golf. Her account in Mowat’s book recalls 96 women responding to the first invitation in February 1998, followed by coaching with Rick Barker and support from member volunteers. She became a Life Member in 2006.

The supplied club notice of 23 February 2023 records her death and remembers her as a driving force behind the success of the nine-hole membership. This later notice extends the record beyond the book’s publication.

life_member_profiles.name: Evelyn “Nen” Sim
paragraphs: In 1974 Nen became the first woman elected to the club executive, standing in open competition with male nominees. She brought experience as handicapper, committee member and writer of the Bunkered women’s golf column.
Her work also supported the club’s social life and twilight catering. She was elected a Life Member in 1985.
life_member_profiles.note: The supplied profile credits Pars from the Past and largely reproduces the account already in the book.
